parole.significato: tight, narrow, cramped (such that it is difficult for something or someone to pass through it; uncomfortably restricted…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahtas (compare Estonian ahas), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *anśtas (compare Lithuanian ankštas), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂énǵʰus.

parole.significato: shaft, thill (one of the poles between which an animal is harnessed to a vehicle)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *aisa (compare Estonian ais), most likely borrowed from Proto-Baltic *ajesa, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂oyHsos. The word has also been compared with Erzya ажия (ažija), which may be a borrowing from Proto-Iranian *Hay(H)ša- (from the same aforementioned Proto-Indo-European word).

parole.significato: eel (any fish in the order Anguilliformes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ankërijas (compare Estonian angerjas), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *angurjás (compare Lithuanian ungurys).

parole.significato: clover (plant in the genus Trifolium)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *apila, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian wobilis (“clover”)).

parole.significato: submerged, dead tree
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hako (compare Estonian hago, Ingrian hako, Karelian hako, Livvi hago, Ludian hago, Veps hago and Votic hako), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šaka (“branch (of a tree)”)).

parole.significato: frost, killing frost (below-freezing temperature that occurs at night during the growing season)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *halla (compare Estonian hall), from earlier *šalna (compare Northern Sami suoldni), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šalnà and Latvian salna).

parole.significato: brush (implement consisting of multiple bristles or other filaments)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *harja (compare Estonian hari, Karelian harja, Livvi harju), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šerys).

parole.significato: grey, gray (colour)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *harmaga, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śirˀmas (compare Lithuanian širmas). Erzya шерже (šerže, “hoar, gray hair”) borrowed from the same root.

parole.significato: tribe
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haimo (compare Estonian hõim), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *šáimas (compare Latvian saime), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱóymos, *tḱóymos.

parole.significato: viburnum (plant of the genus Viburnum)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *häici (“flower, inflorescence”) (compare Estonian õis (“flower”)), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian žiedas). The words heitiä and hedelmä (“fruit”) are derived from the same Proto-Finnic root. The modern meaning "viburnum" is a backformation from heisipuu.

parole.significato: hot weather, swelter
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *heldeh (compare Karelian helleh), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šiltis).

parole.significato: hornet (Vespa)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *herhiläinen (compare Estonian herilane (“wasp”)), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śirˀšṓ (compare Lithuanian širšė) and derived with *-läinen.

parole.significato: heifer (young female cow, particularly one which has not yet calved)
parole.testo: PIE word  *h₁éḱwos From Proto-Finnic *hëhva (compare dialectal hiehvo, Estonian õhv, Livonian õ’v, Votic õhvõ), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *éśwāˀ (compare Lithuanian ašva (“mare”)).

parole.significato: strap, band; especially one that is made of leather or other strong material
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hihna, from earlier *ši(k)šna, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian šikšnà (“strap, belt, leather”)), if the Baltic and Finnic words are not from a substrate. Related to Erzya кшна (kšna, “strap”) (of the same origin).

parole.significato: price (cost to purchase; cost of an action)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hinta (compare Estonian hind), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *śímta (compare Lithuanian šimtas (“hundred”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱm̥tóm (“hundred”), and thereby a distant doublet of sata. However, the Baltic etymology is uncertain, since the semantic develop

parole.significato: elk, moose (Alces alces)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hirvi (compare Estonian hirv, Veps hirbʹ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *širˀwis (compare Old Prussian sirwis (“deer”), Proto-Balto-Slavic *śírˀnāˀ (“roe deer”)), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂- (“head, top, horn”) (compare Latin cervus). Doublet of sarvi.

parole.significato: to blind, dazzle
parole.testo: häikä- + -äistä, from the stem *häikä-, akin to Ingrian häjätä, Karelian häijätä, Votic häigete (probably borrowed from another Finnic language), from Proto-Finnic *häikä-. If it goes back to a root *häi-, it could possibly be a loan from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian seja), an etymology ori

parole.significato: hoar frost, hoarfrost
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *härmä (compare Estonian härm, Karelian härmä, Livonian ǟrma; from earlier *šärmä), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian sarma, Lithuanian šarma).

parole.significato: detachable, removable, separate, loose
parole.testo: From *irta + -i (irto- < *irtoi < *irta-i), from Proto-Finnic *irta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian irti (“to fall apart, to separate”)).

parole.significato: beast of burden
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jukta, probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian jūgt), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *yugtós; see the Proto-Finnic entry for more.

parole.significato: leash of a yoke
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *jutta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *jutas.

parole.significato: everything (in the singular)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaikki, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kajakei.

parole.significato: namesake (a person with the same name as another person)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaima (compare Estonian kaim, Proto-Samic *kuojmē), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian káimas, Latvian ciems). Northern Sami gaiˈbmât (“to adapt to a companion, to enjoy company”), from Proto-Samic *kājmē, is a later borrowing from Finnic.

parole.significato: stanchion; a support between a skid and the frame on a sleigh
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kaplas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian kablis, Lithuanian kablys).

parole.significato: card (comb- or brush-like device or tool to raise the nap on a fabric)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karsta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian karsti).

parole.significato: Any lichen of the family Parmeliaceae; parmeliaceous lichen.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *karbëk, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian karpitnes (“lichen”)).

parole.significato: ladle, dipper (cup-shaped vessel with a long handle, for dipping out liquids)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kauha, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *káuˀ-, from Proto-Indo-European *kowh₂-, from the root *kewh₂-. Compare Lithuanian káušas (“ladle, dipper, big spoon”).

parole.significato: neck (part of the body connecting the head and the trunk)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kakla (compare Estonian kael), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kaklas (compare Lithuanian kaklas). Distant doublet of chakra, kekri, and sykli.

parole.significato: top rail; beam above and parallel to the runner that holds the tops of the supports between the skid and the frame on a…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kausta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *skaustas (whence Latvian skausts).

parole.significato: reel, spool, bobbin (device around which thread, wire, cable or something similar is wound)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këla, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian kelan (“wheel”)).

parole.significato: weather conditions relating specifically to surfaces for travel (such as road conditions or skiing conditions)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *keli, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *keljas (compare Latvian ceļš (“road”), Lithuanian kelias (“road”)).

parole.significato: yellow
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këlta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *gilˀtos (compare Lithuanian geltas). May be a distant doublet of kulta.

parole.significato: time, occasion (particular instance or occurrence)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kërta (compare Estonian kord), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kartas (compare Old Prussian kērdan (accusative singular), Lithuanian kartas), although other Indo-European etyma have also been proposed (see the Proto-Finnic entry for more).

parole.significato: synonym of kaplas
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *këtara, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian ketera, ketaras). Erzya кодор (kodor, “stake, plant’s stake”) borrowed from the same Baltic root.

parole.significato: mitten, mitt (type of glove or garment that covers a hand with a separate sheath for the thumb, but not for other finge…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kindas (compare Estonian kinnas, Ingrian kinnas, Karelian kinnaš, Livonian kīndaz, Ludian kindaz, Veps kindaz, Votic činnõz), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kimdas (compare Latvian cimds).

parole.significato: ground frost (frozen top layer of soil caused by cold weather in winter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirci (compare Estonian kirs, Ingrian kersi, Karelian kirsi, Livonian kirt), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian apskirsti (“to freeze”)).

parole.significato: axe (tool)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kirves (compare Estonian kirves), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian cirvis, Lithuanian kirvis).

parole.significato: culm; stem of a grass or sedge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *korci, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *karti (compare Lithuanian kartis (“thin rod, mowing, raking”)).

parole.significato: an evil being
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kouko (compare Estonian kõuk), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian kaukas).

parole.significato: dry, dead grass from the previous summer
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kulo, probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian kūla (“dry grass”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *keh₂w-.

parole.significato: sheaf (bundle of straw)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kupo, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian guba and Lithuanian guba).

parole.significato: helmet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *küpärä (“hat”), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *kepur- (compare Latvian cepure (“hat”)).

parole.significato: bay, gulf, inlet (portion of a body of water extending into the land)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lakci (compare Karelian laksi, Veps laht, Estonian laht, Votic lahti, Northern Sami luokta), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian lanktis (“arc”)). -ht- in the nominative is by analogy with the oblique case forms; the expected form laksi (compare the declension o

parole.significato: A type of trap for hunting birds, especially grouses.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lahto, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?].

parole.significato: a tool with a handle and a wide, flat blade
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lasta, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian lazda (“hazel”)), as hazelwood was a common material for utensils.

parole.significato: sad
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leinä + -o, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?].

parole.significato: alder (any of the trees in the genus Alnus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leppä (compare Estonian lepp, Veps lep), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *léiˀpāˀ (“linden tree”) (compare Latvian liepa), if the Finnic and Baltic words are not of common substrate origin. Also related to Erzya лепе (lepe). * (blood): Euphemistic; refers to the fact that the

parole.significato: hem, skirt (the lower edge of a garment)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *leebek (compare Veps ĺebe), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian klēpis (“lap”)).

parole.significato: excess, overabundance, glut (the state of being excessive or too much, or that which is excessive or too much)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liika (compare Estonian liig, Karelian liika, Veps liig, Votic liikõ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian lieks), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *leykʷ-. Erzya лия (lija, “other, else”) possibly borrowed from the same root.

parole.significato: salmon (fish of the family Salmonidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lohi, from earlier *loši, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *laśas.

parole.significato: to mine (remove ore from the ground)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *louhidak (compare Karelian louhie), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (*laužija, compare Lithuanian láužti, Latvian lauzt). * (to mine (in computing)): Semantic loan from English mine.

parole.significato: water lily (a flower of the genus Nymphaea)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lumbëh (compare Karelian lummeh and Võro lymmuleht'), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *lugmis (compare Lithuanian lugmiai).

parole.significato: roof pole (on a birchbark or straw roof); a (thin) wooden pole or beam that extends from the ridge to the eave, with su…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malka, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian malka (“firewood, splinter”), Lithuanian malka (“firewood, splinter, log”)).

parole.significato: forest, woods
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *meccä (compare Estonian mets, Ludian mecc, Veps mec, Võro mõts), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *medjas (compare Latvian mežs, Lithuanian medis).

parole.significato: blackfly, buffalo gnat (any insect of the family Simuliidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäkärä (probably from earlier *makara), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian makatas (“gnat”)). Cognate with dialectal Estonian mägar, Karelian mäkärä, Ludian mägär and Proto-Samic *muokēr.

parole.significato: piston (solid disk or cylinder that fits inside a hollow cylinder)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *mäntä, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian mente). The original senses were for mixing and stirring utensils; the mechanical sense “piston” (probably 19th century) is from “plunger, dasher, churn-staff”.

parole.significato: wet
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *märkä (compare Estonian märg), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian mērka (“humidity”)).

parole.significato: A first cousin.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nëpada, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Old Lithuanian nepuotis), from Proto-Indo-European *népōts. Cognate with Estonian nõbu.

parole.significato: heddle, heald (part of a loom)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *niici, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian nīts, Lithuanian nytis).

parole.significato: thorn, prickle
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ogas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?]. Compare Estonian oga, Ingrian oaz and Veps ogah.

parole.significato: a wooden beam or bar on which objects, such as tools, are hung from when they are not used
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *orci, from earlier *orti, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian ar̃das (“pole scaffold for drying flax”)).

parole.significato: fire
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *panu, probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic *panu (compare Old Prussian panno (“fire”)).

parole.significato: to disparage, defame, slander
parole.testo: Unknown. Possibly from Proto-Finnic *parjat'ak, which could be from Proto-Baltic *bárˀtei (compare Latvian bārt, Lithuanian barti), or a blend of paaruta or paasata and herjata.

parole.significato: porridge
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *putro (compare Estonian puder, Karelian putro, Veps pudr), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian putra (“porridge”)).

parole.significato: crack, chink, fissure, slit (narrow opening)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rako (compare Estonian pragu, Ingrian rako, Karelian rako, Votic rako), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian spraga, Lithuanian spraga).

parole.significato: thrush (any of several species of songbirds of the family Turdidae)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rastas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *trazdas, compare Latvian strazds (“starling, thrush”) and Lithuanian strazdas (“thrush”), from Proto-Indo-European *trosdos.

parole.significato: edge, brink, rim, border, brim, fringe, verge, boundary (outer boundary line of something)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rëuna (compare Karelian reuna, Ludian reun, Veps röun), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian briauna).

parole.significato: to grind coarsely, crush, kibble
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rouhidak (compare Livvi rouhie, Ludian rouhida, Veps rouhta), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian krausēt, Lithuanian kraušyti (“to strike”)), from Proto-Indo-European *krus- (compare Ancient Greek κρούω (kroúō), Proto-Germanic *hrusǭ).

parole.significato: ground frost (frozen top layer of soil caused by cold weather in winter)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *routa, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian grúodas (“frost, frozen street dirt”)).

parole.significato: chaff, husk(s) (inedible parts removed from cereal during threshing)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ruumën (compare Ingrian rummen, Karelian ruumen, Veps rumen), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *grūdmen-.

parole.significato: group (number of things or persons being in some relation to each other)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rühmä (compare Estonian rühm), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian trūkšmas).

parole.significato: sleet; rain and snow mixed, wet snow (a mixture of rain and snow)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *räntä, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian drengti).

parole.significato: point (sharp tip, e.g. of a star)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sakara (compare Estonian sagar, Karelian sakara, Ludian sagar, Veps tšagar, Votic sakarõ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian stãgaras).

parole.significato: dace, Leuciscus leuciscus
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *seipi, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *steip-.

parole.significato: pole, stake (long and slender piece of wood or other material, pointed at one end so as to be easily driven into the gr…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *saibas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *staipas (compare Lithuanian sti̇́ebas). Cognates include Estonian teivas, Livonian tāibaz, Ludian šeibäz, Veps seibaz, Võro saivass and Votic seivez.

parole.significato: company (visitors, companionship)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sëpra (compare Estonian sõber), probably borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian sēbrs (“friend”), Lithuanian sėbras (“companion”)). Erzya шабра (šabra) is possibly borrowed from the same source.

parole.significato: seed (fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *seemen, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *sḗˀmin, from Proto-Indo-European *séh₁mn̥. Doublet of hieman.

parole.significato: awn
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ciika(inën) ( + -(i)nen), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *dīgas (whence Lithuanian dygas (“thorn”)).

parole.significato: bridge (construction or natural feature that spans a divide)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cilta, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *tílˀta (compare Latvian tilts, Lithuanian tiltas).

parole.significato: a net or mesh in a wing of a seine that is located on the far end; side net or mesh in a seine; outer mesh of a fishing…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *cikla (compare Karelian šikla), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian tìkls and Lithuanian tinklas).

parole.significato: haystack
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *soova, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian stāvs (“stature, storey”), Lithuanian stovas (“rack, stand”)).

parole.significato: edge, side
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sürjä, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic *sturjas (compare Latvian stūris (“corner”), dialectal Lithuanian stūrỹs, stùris (“corner”)).

parole.significato: dense, thick, crowded, packed
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *takja (compare Karelian toakie and also Northern Sami dávjá), possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian tankus).

parole.significato: bee, dugnad (gathering for carrying out a major task, such as harvesting, construction or cleaning)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *talko- (compare Estonian talgud, Karelian talloh, Veps touguh, Votic talko), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *talkōs (compare Lithuanian talka (“cooperated voluntary work”)).

parole.significato: habit (action performed on a regular basis)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tapa, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *dabāˀ (compare Latvian daba).

parole.significato: to snatch, grab, jerk, pull, tear, yank
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tëmbait'ak (compare Karelian temmata, Ingrian temmata, Votic tõmmõtõ, Estonian tõmbama, Ludian tembaita, Veps tembaita), likely borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian tempt, Lithuanian tempti).

parole.significato: A small dam, usually made of logs.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *togëh, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *takis, compare Lithuanian takišys, Latvian tacis.

parole.significato: horn (any of several musical wind instruments, especially one used to signal people or animals)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *torvi (compare Estonian tõri, Karelian torvi, Veps torv), from earlier *towre (with metathesis *wr > *rw, compare järvi, karva), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian taure (“bugle”)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *táwros. Doublet of Taurus, tarvas, and teuras

parole.significato: thousand
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuhat, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *tū́ˀsantis (compare Lithuanian tūkstantis), from Proto-Indo-European *tuHsont-.

parole.significato: synonym of atrain (“gig”) (forked spear)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuulas, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Latvian dūlājs, Lithuanian dūlis).

parole.significato: ice chisel; a tool for breaking ice, consisting of a heavy chisel-like iron head which is attached to a long wooden han…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuura (compare Estonian tuur, Ingrian tuura, Võro tuur, Votic tuurõ), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian durà).

parole.significato: daughter
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tüt'är, borrowed from Proto-Baltic *duktē (compare Lithuanian duktė). Erzya тейтерь (tejteŕ) may be borrowed from the same source.

parole.significato: wasp, bee
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vapsa-, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian vapsva and Old Prussian wobse). Cognate with Estonian vapsik, Karelian voapsahaine, Livonian vaps, Veps bapshaine and Votic vaapsõlain.

parole.significato: A roundish, voluminous container equipped with a cap.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vakka, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vāks (“lid, cover”), Lithuanian vókas (“cover, eyelid”)).

parole.significato: furrow (trench cut in the soil)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vako (compare Estonian vagu), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vaga (“furrow”)).

parole.significato: harness (restraint or support consisting of a loop or network of rope or straps)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *valjas, possibly borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Old Prussian walis (“drawbar”)). Cognate to Estonian valjad (“headstall”), Estonian valjastada, Ingrian valjaat, Votic valʹlʹad (“bridle”), Karelian vaľľahad, Ludian vaľľahad, Veps vaľľastuz.

parole.significato: early
parole.testo: Through metathesis, from Proto-Finnic *varahin, the instructive plural of Proto-Finnic *varas (compare dialectal Finnish varas, Livonian varāz, Veps varaz, Votic varaz), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *vāras (compare Lithuanian võras (“old”)). Related to Estonian vara, Ingrian varahiin, Karelian varahin

parole.significato: yet (thus far)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *veelä (compare Estonian veel), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian vēl (“yet, still, again”), Lithuanian vėl (“again”)).

parole.significato: rush (any plant of the genus Juncus)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *vihvilä, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian viksva (“sedge”)).

parole.significato: wool
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *villa (compare Estonian vill), borrowed from Proto-Baltic *wílˀnāˀ (compare Lithuanian vi̇̀lna, Polish wełna), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂ (compare English wool, French laine).

parole.significato: line or row, especially of traps or snares
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *virka, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Latvian verdze).

parole.significato: kid (young goat)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voohla (from earlier *(v)oošëla), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian oželis), if not a native *-la diminutive of *voohi.

parole.significato: hide, pelt (removed but otherwise untreated skin of an animal, particularly a large animal)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *voota, borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (compare Lithuanian oda).

parole.significato: chewing louse (any louse of the obsolete suborder Mallophaga)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *väiveh (compare Estonian väiv, Karelian väiveh, Votic väive), borrowed from Proto-Baltic [Term?] (whence Lithuanian vievesà).
